description:
About the Position

Surrey Morphology Group is recruiting a PhD student to compare predictability in Romance verbal inflection.

The studentship forms part of the UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship project Scaling Predictability in Morphological Paradigms.

Official Project Title

Fully funded PhD studentship on predictability in Romance verbal inflection

Research Focus and Methods

Develop and apply computational measures of the information speakers use to infer word forms. Compare contemporary and historical Romance datasets to investigate how morphological predictability varies and changes.

Research Training and Development

Computational methodology can be learned during the project; prior technical expertise is not required.

Funding and Duration

Studentship funding and award conditions
ComponentDetails
AwardPhD studentship; selection is competitive
ProgrammeSurrey studentship
Duration42 months (3.5 years)
StipendUKRI-rate living stipend. The programme quotes £21,805 per year for 2026/27; the 2027/28 rate is not yet published on the checked funding page.
Tuition and research supportUK or international tuition fees, UKRI-rate stipend and conference-travel support.
Award conditionsSelection is competitive; an advertised project does not guarantee a studentship.
Stipend amount status£21,805 is the published 2026/27 reference rate. Subsequent academic-year rates and the amount in an individual funding offer should be checked separately.

Eligibility and English Language

Applicant qualifications and funding eligibility
ComponentDetails
Applicant eligibilityWorldwide applicants may apply, subject to programme and university requirements.
Academic preparationExcellent undergraduate performance, expertise in morphological description and analysis, and familiarity with Romance linguistics.
Project interests and skillsMorphological analysis and familiarity with Romance linguistics are selection criteria.
English languageMeet the host university’s English-language admission rules. An approved alternative or exemption may apply; IELTS is not universally mandatory.

About University of Surrey

University of Surrey is a public research university in Guildford, England. It offers undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral programmes across engineering, science, business, health, humanities and social sciences. Its teaching and research connect academic foundations with professional practice, supported by partnerships and work addressing questions in technology, health and contemporary society.

Official website: https://www.surrey.ac.uk/

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be sent to the contacts above or raised through the channel given on the official announcement page.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 20 December 2026 - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

How to Apply

  1. Apply through Surrey’s Linguistics PhD programme, linked in the advert.
  2. Also email a CV and a one-page statement of interest to a.stubley@surrey.ac.uk, naming the project and supervisors.

  • Supporting documents requested by the Linguistics PhD application system
